rows.text: Everybody’s missing Tao’s whole point. Imagine an AI-generated cancer drug that’s specifically designed to game the drug trial process. The drug makes the cancer cells go dormant and changes the way they appear in blood tests and diagnostic imaging, such that they become indistinguishable from healthy tissue. The drug clears the trial and then only much later do we find out it didn’t work. It probably was also harmful on top of that. We *already* see AI behave like that when confronted with difficult programming/hacking challenges. This is already reality.

rows.text: I’m in Paris with @XPENG_Global ahead of the Motor Show and got to experience its driving assistance system on the city’s streets. I got to experience XPENG’s NGP on European roads for the first time, here in Paris. Super smooth, even with roadworks and traffic jams. I was surprised by how well it handled Paris traffic. XPENG and Tesla will be the only two automakers participating in the show’s official Autonomous Lab, offering supervised rides on public roads. Really enjoyed experiencing this firsthand. Looking forward to more FSD in europe!
